_doc: Which files deserve a word of caution before someone opens one they were sent (2026-10-17, from a suggestion in the project's Discord: say when a file is a program, a script, an archive and so on, and to scan it first). Read by the desktop app (src/net/file_risk.rs) and the website (web/shared/file-risk.js), the same way, from this one list. Not an antivirus: it reads a file's name and its first bytes, and says what kind of thing it is and what to be careful of. `extensions` are lower case without the dot, longest first where one ends another (tar.gz before gz). `magic` is the file's first bytes, in lower-case hex: a file whose name says one kind and whose bytes say a program or an archive is called out as disguised (`named_as` lists the kinds a name can claim, and which kinds of contents would make it a disguise). Words: {ext} is the file's ending, {claimed} and {actual} are names from this file.

kinds.name: a program
kinds.words: This is a program ({ext}). A program can do anything on your computer: only run it if you trust the person it came from, and scan it with your antivirus first.

kinds.name: a script
kinds.words: This is a script ({ext}). A script runs commands on your computer when it is opened: only run it if you trust the person it came from, and read it or scan it first.

kinds.name: an archive
kinds.words: This is an archive ({ext}). What is inside it has not been checked: scan it with your antivirus before you open what it holds, and be careful with any program inside.

kinds.name: a document that can carry macros
kinds.words: This document can carry macros ({ext}). If it asks you to turn on macros or editing, do not, unless you trust the person it came from.

kinds.name: a shortcut
kinds.words: This is a shortcut ({ext}). A shortcut can start a program or open a website without saying which: do not open it unless you trust the person it came from.

kinds.name: a web page
kinds.words: This is a web page or markup file ({ext}). Opened, it runs in your browser with its own scripts: do not open it unless you trust the person it came from.

kinds.name: a Blender file
kinds.words: Blender files can carry scripts. If Blender asks whether to run them, say no unless you trust the person who shared it.

disguised: This file is named like {claimed} ({ext}), but what is inside is {actual}. Do not open it: a file pretending to be something else is a common trick.
